    def test_urlsplit_port_validation(self):
        # Construction (urlsplit) always succeeds; only .port access raises.
        # --- text URLs ---
        # no port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com/")
        self.assertIsNone(p.port)

        # empty port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:/")
        self.assertIsNone(p.port)

        # port 0
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:0/")
        self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)

        # port 65535
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:65535/")
        self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)

        # port 65536: out of range
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:65536/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         ("Port out of range 0-65535",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         "Port out of range 0-65535")

        # negative port: not a valid digit string
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:-1/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         ("Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         "Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'")

        # non-integer port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:abc/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         ("Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         "Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'")

        # non-ASCII decimal digit (Arabic-Indic DIGIT ONE, U+0661)
        digit = "\u0661"
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit("http://example.com:" + digit + "/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         (f"Port could not be cast to integer value as {digit!r}",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         f"Port could not be cast to integer value as {digit!r}")

        # --- bytes URLs ---
        # no port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com/")
        self.assertIsNone(p.port)

        # empty port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com:/")
        self.assertIsNone(p.port)

        # port 0
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com:0/")
        self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)

        # port 65535
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com:65535/")
        self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)

        # port 65536: out of range
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com:65536/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         ("Port out of range 0-65535",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         "Port out of range 0-65535")

        # negative port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com:-1/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         ("Port could not be cast to integer value as b'-1'",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         "Port could not be cast to integer value as b'-1'")

        # non-integer port
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(b"http://example.com:abc/")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            p.port
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args,
                         ("Port could not be cast to integer value as b'abc'",))
        self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception),
                         "Port could not be cast to integer value as b'abc'")
